verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep the original order of steps and side effects (tax lookup, coupon check, reservation, charge, commit and redeem, receipt), so production behavior is preserved in both. B also adds characterization tests for the paths the existing suite misses: VIP stacking, the free-shipping boundary, per-line rounding, invalid coupon and quantity, partial release, and no coupon redemption on decline. B confirmed these tests passed on the original code and they hold up when checked by hand. A refactored a production function with thin test coverage and only told the reviewer to check coverage themselves.
a_issues: No tests added, although the existing suite does not cover VIP, invalid-coupon, invalid-quantity, partial-release or notifier-failure paths for a production refactor.
`_charge` signature is one overly long line, and `list` is used without an element type in the helper signatures.
The report leaves coverage verification to the developer instead of doing it.
b_issues: `_charge` takes six parameters, which is a slightly awkward helper boundary (A shares this).
The free-shipping test name mentions discounts but exercises no discount.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior the same: helper boundaries, call order (tax lookup, coupon check, reservation, charge, commit, redeem, notify), error messages, statuses and exception chaining all match the original. A adds 11 characterization tests, confirmed against the original code before refactoring. They pin the paths the existing suite misses: VIP stacked on a coupon, the free-shipping boundary, per-line rounding, partial-reservation release, no coupon redemption on decline, and a failing notifier. B relies only on the 9 existing tests and leaves coverage for the reviewer to check, which is weak protection for a refactor of live production code.
a_issues: Adds about 90 lines of tests in the same PR. They are useful as characterization tests, but they make the diff larger than the refactor itself.
`_charge` takes six parameters, which is somewhat clunky.
b_issues: Adds no tests, even though the existing suite does not cover VIP discounts, the shipping boundary, per-line rounding, partial-reservation release or notifier failure.
Moves `process_order` below the helpers, so the diff is noisier than needed and the entry point is harder to find.
Uses a bare `list` type for `reserved` instead of `list[Item]`, and the `_charge` signature is an over-long single line.
The extra `_shipping` helper is a one-line function that adds little.
